title: Why does the rig run several times faster than a lived-in fort? Ticks per wall second, tick cap 1000, on the 7-dwarf CTRL and on BOATS (the copy of the user's live Boatsbowed fort, 30 dwarves), with the graphics cap at 10 or 60, and the tool on or off on BOATS. Throughput is the harness's ticks / wall seconds per 1,000-tick step, first step discarded.
fork: How much of the gap between the rig (~150-400 t/s) and the user's live play (~30 FPS at 60 GFPS) is fort load, the graphics cap, and the tool.

predictions.expects: BOATS far slower than CTRL at either graphics cap
gfps 60 far slower than gfps 10 on both forts

predictions.model: the tool is a small cost
predictions.expects: BOATS tool off within ~10-15% of tool on (E38 measured 10-12%)

kill_criterion: a replicate whose achieved gfps never reaches its cap's neighbourhood did not test the cap
culling: the first 1,000-tick step of every replicate (warm-up, load-time caches)

arms.name: A_ctrl_g10
pre: local sw=reqscript('seasonal-wildlife'); local cfg=sw.loadConfig(); if not cfg.initialized then sw.captureDefault(cfg) end; cfg.enabled=true; cfg.groups.enabled=true; sw.saveConfig(cfg); sw.enableSched(); print('fps1: tool on')

local e=df.global.enabler; local w=df.global.world; local n=0; for _,u in ipairs(w.units.active) do if dfhack.units.isCitizen(u) then n=n+1 end end; print(('fps1 load: citizens %d units %d items %d map %dx%dx%d fps %s gfps %s caps %s/%s'):format(n, #w.units.active, #w.items.other.IN_PLAY, w.map.x_count, w.map.y_count, w.map.z_count, tostring(e.calculated_fps), tostring(e.calculated_gfps), tostring(e.fps), tostring(e.gfps)))
